title: Number parsing, validation and range expansion
summary: E.164 normalization and turning rules into exact number lists for iOS
description:
CURRENT STATE: nothing built in Rust. The arithmetic is proven by throwaway Python prototypes in the session scratchpad (expand.py, generic.py) which ran against real libphonenumber metadata across all 245 territories; those are reference only.

NORMALIZATION: normalize(raw, defaultRegion) -> E164. Use the `phonenumber` crate (0.3.10+9.0.33) for parse/validate/format.

EXPANSION — the part iOS calls depend on: expand(Rule, limit) -> sorted exact numbers, or TooBroad(count). Driven by possibleLengths AND nationalNumberPattern, per country per number type, from F003's datasets.

THE REGEX MUST PRUNE. Summing possible lengths alone materially overestimates. Worst case measured: DE fixedLine has ELEVEN possible lengths (5 to 15), so a naive sum gives 11,111,111,111,000 for "+49 30" where the validating pattern rejects most of it. The prototype only summed lengths and is knowingly wrong here — the real implementation must apply the pattern.

ALLOW-EXCEPTIONS BY SUBTRACTION: CallKit has no allow list, so an allow rule inside a deny is resolved here by simply not emitting that number — 999 entries instead of 1000. No runtime support needed on iOS.

OUTPUT ORDER: iOS requires strictly ascending int64 with no duplicates (addBlockingEntry(withNextSequentialPhoneNumber:)). Generate in order and assert monotonicity — an out-of-order entry fails the whole extension request.

STREAMING, NOT MATERIALISING: the iOS extension runs under tight memory limits, so expansion must yield incrementally rather than build a full Vec.

THE LIMIT IS INJECTED: the maximum entry count comes from F001's measurement as configuration, never a constant (Guidelines §4). explain(Rule) returns the expansion count and per-platform verdict for R2's honesty requirement.

MEASURED CONTEXT: 226/244 countries need <=4 digits pinned for mobile, 223/245 for landline. Hard tail: DE fixedLine 10 digits, AT mobile 8, DE mobile 6, IT fixedLine 7.
